detail: Between 5% and 10% below the high counts as a pullback, and the S&P 500 closed at 7,416.59 on Monday, about 5.1% below its record close of 7,818.93 on 6 October. It has fallen three days running as chip shares slid; dips of this size happen in most years.
source: CNBC and AP closing figures, 16 Nov; record close from Anadolu and EdgeX, 6 Oct

detail: Breadth was narrow on Monday: at midday Reuters counted 366 Nasdaq shares at new 52-week lows against just 35 at new highs, with fallers outnumbering risers by about 2.7 to 1. When most shares fall together, the selling is wide rather than limited to a few big names.
source: Reuters midday breadth snapshot via FXNews, 16 Nov

detail: Above 4.5% counts as high, and the US 10-year yield eased to about 5.12% on Monday from 5.15% as investors bought safe bonds during the share sell-off. Safe government bonds paying over 5% set a high bar for shares to beat.
source: US Treasury closing yield via Ausecure; Barchart (5.115%), 16 Nov

detail: Markets expect rates to go up: futures price a quarter-point Fed rise on 9 December as close to certain, and Bank of England chief economist Huw Pill said the Bank has further to go on rate rises. Higher rates make borrowing dearer and tend to weigh on share prices, especially fast-growing companies.
source: Fed funds futures via Barchart, 16 Nov; Huw Pill to the FT via Alliance News, 16 Nov

detail: Above $90 a barrel counts as expensive, even after Monday's 3.6% fall: Brent crude settled at $92.44 as more oil flowed through the Strait of Hormuz. Dear oil keeps pressure on inflation, which is one reason central banks are raising rates.
source: ICE settlement via Dow Jones Market Data and CNBC, 16 Nov
